research_objective: Validate claim: '20k-50k professional machinists paying $50-300/year for feeds/speeds calculators'
research_methodology: Hard data from BLS, app analytics, web search, app store metrics
data_quality_assessment: MIXED - Some authoritative sources (BLS, app store metrics) mixed with industry claims lacking public verification

ios.note: Very low review count suggests either small user base or poor review prompting

windows.note: Installation count does not equal active users

fswizard.developer_responsiveness: Very positive - frequently praised in forums

claim_2.text: Over 100,000 machinists from thousands of companies use G-Wizard

historical_active_data.note: Historical data, not current; only counts people who logged in

gwizard.company_status: Founder Bob Warfield passed away 2024; new ownership unclear about license sales capability

hsmadvisor.basis_for_estimate: App analytics platforms do not publish HSMAdvisor numbers; developer does not disclose metrics; inferred from user sentiment and adoption discussions
hsmadvisor.note: Lack of public data may indicate smaller user base than competitors, or developer preference for privacy
hsmadvisor.growth_indicator: Forum discussions show migration FROM G-Wizard TO HSMAdvisor, but no quantity data

total_market_paying_users_estimate.basis: FSWizard paying (~1200), G-Wizard subscribers (~12000), HSMAdvisor (~5000-8000), Other competitors (~3000-5000)
total_market_paying_users_estimate.assessment: ORIGINAL CLAIM OF 20K-50K IS AT UPPER BOUNDARY OR SLIGHTLY OPTIMISTIC

global_cnc_employment.note: Asia Pacific dominates market but individual country employment data not publicly available

review_engagement_rates.source: Academic and industry research on app review behavior
review_engagement_rates.key_insight: FSWizard shows HIGHER than typical free app review rate, suggesting either high quality/satisfaction OR active review prompting

fswizard_ios_analysis.red_flag: Only 32 reviews after 12 years on App Store suggests either very small iOS user base or poor review prompting; comparable to small niche apps
fswizard_ios_analysis.implication: iOS version likely underperforming compared to Android

download_to_active_user_conversion.basis: Typical mobile app MAU is 5-30% of total installs depending on category; calculator apps tend lower (specialized tools)

cnc_machines_in_operation_usa.total_estimated: Unknown - market research focuses on monetary value not unit count
cnc_machines_in_operation_usa.market_size_source: Fortune Business Insights, Allied Market Research
cnc_machines_in_operation_usa.note: Cannot determine installed base from market dollar size

machine_shop_distribution.distribution: Highly skewed - many 1-5 person shops, fewer 50+ person shops

cnc_market_size.note: Large market size in dollars but unclear how many individual users/shops this represents

feeds_speeds_calculator_usage.estimate: Unknown - no public survey data found
feeds_speeds_calculator_usage.implied_rate_from_app_data: 5-10% of machinists use dedicated calculator software
feeds_speeds_calculator_usage.basis: FSWizard + G-Wizard + HSMAdvisor total ~25k-35k active users vs 299k machinists = ~8-12%

paid_specialty_software_adoption.basis: Limited data; inferred from: (1) market research showing 54% of manufacturers increase tech spend, (2) app pricing barriers

willing_to_pay_segment.source: Forum analysis and app review sentiment

reality_check.original_claim: 20,000-50,000 professional machinists paying $50-300/year for feeds/speeds calculators
reality_check.claim_assessment: PARTIALLY VALIDATED - upper bound plausible, but middle-to-lower range more likely

validated_range.basis: FSWizard (~1200-1600 paying), G-Wizard (~10000-15000 paying), HSMAdvisor (~5000-8000 paying), Others (~3000-5000)

reality_check.confidence_level: MEDIUM - Data exists but is incomplete; some assumptions required
key_findings: Total US machinists: ~299,500 (hard data from BLS)
CNC specialists specifically: ~187,670 (hard data from BLS)
Global CNC professionals: ~1-2.5 million (estimate; incomplete data)
Known app users estimates: FSWizard ~2-3k active, G-Wizard ~10-15k, HSMAdvisor ~5-10k = ~17-28k total
Market share of professional machinists using paid calculators: ~5-12%
Very few apps disclose user numbers; must infer from app store metrics
FSWizard's iOS presence is surprisingly weak (32 reviews) for 12-year-old app
key_assumptions: Active users = estimated from review counts using 0.1% baseline engagement rate
Paying users = estimated at 50-80% of active users for paid apps
Monthly active rate = 0.5-1% of total installs for specialized calculator apps
G-Wizard's '100,000' claim includes all trial users ever created, not active paying subscribers
HSMAdvisor user base estimated from silence (no public disclosure usually means smaller numbers)
red_flags: FSWizard iOS: Only 32 reviews after 12 years - suggests minimal iOS market penetration despite being on main App Store
G-Wizard dual claims: '15,000 pros' vs '100,000 machinists' indicates marketing inflation of larger number
No HSMAdvisor public metrics: May indicate developer preference for privacy OR smaller user base than competitors
CNCCookbook founder passed away (2024): Current status of G-Wizard sales/support unclear - may impact current subscriber count
App review rate inconsistency: FSWizard shows 0.325% (free) to 3.45% (paid) - unusually high suggests small user base showing high quality rather than volume
Downloads ≠ Active Users: FSWizard's 240k free downloads likely represents only 2-4k monthly active users based on industry engagement rates
reality_check.question_validity_assessment: The '20k-50k paying professional machinists' claim is AT THE UPPER BOUNDARY of market data but not refuted by available evidence. More likely range: 20k-35k paying users globally (not just US), representing ~6-12% of professional machinists

supporting_evidence: 299,500 machinists in US represents addressable market
Global market of 1-2.5 million provides larger opportunity
Professional shops have documented willingness to pay $50-300/year for tools
G-Wizard's historical 10,000 active users (2019-2020) validates mid-range estimate
Dedicated calculator app category shows some market traction (not dead category)
contradicting_evidence: FSWizard shows weak engagement: only 32 iOS reviews after 12 years
Total visible market (FSWizard + G-Wizard + HSMAdvisor) appears ~20-35k, not 50k+
Review engagement rates suggest far more downloads than active users
Many machinists still use free/alternative methods (Handbook, CAM software, experience)
No public disclosure of user numbers by any vendor (transparency problem suggests smaller numbers than marketing claims)
investment_implications: Market is real but smaller than claimed - 20k-35k professional paying users is realistic global baseline
Market may grow IF product offers significant innovation over existing tools
High professionalism/specialization needed - must target actual paying professionals, not hobbyists
Competitive advantage required: FSWizard dominates free/cheap, G-Wizard dominates mid-market; need clear differentiation
Customer acquisition cost may be high given small addressable market and high user research intensity

high_confidence_sources: BLS Employment Data: 299,500 machinists (official government data)
App Store Metrics: FSWizard downloads and reviews (direct from public stores)
IBISWorld Industry Data: 16,817 machine shops in US (business intelligence firm)
CNCCookbook G-Wizard Claims: 15,000 users (company claim, but contradicted by other claims)
medium_confidence_sources: App Analytics (0.1% review engagement baseline): Used for estimating active users from reviews
G-Wizard historical active data: 10,000 Windows users logged in over 6 months (2019-2020)
Forum sentiment analysis: Indicates demand and user preferences
Industry trend reports: Market growth, adoption patterns
low_confidence_sources: HSMAdvisor user estimates: Inferred from silence; no public data
Global CNC machinist count: Only partial country data available
Percentage of machinists using calculators: No survey data found
Customer acquisition costs and LTV: Not researched
gaps_in_data: No public subscriber numbers for any paid calculator software
No survey of machinists on software tool spending habits
No installed base count of CNC machines globally
No breakdown of shop size vs software adoption correlation
No data on willingness to pay vs. feature set (price elasticity unknown)

recommendations_for_validation: Contact G-Wizard/CNCCookbook new ownership for current subscriber count verification
Contact Eldar Gerfanov (FSWizard/HSMAdvisor) for user base disclosure or partnership discussion
Conduct 20-30 machinist interviews across different shop types and sizes to validate software adoption %
Request app analytics data from Sensor Tower or similar if budget allows ($500-2000)
Survey manufacturing forums (Practical Machinist, CNCZone) on calculator usage and software spending
Analyze CAM software adoption rates (Fusion 360 at 67% adoption rate) as ceiling for potential market share
Research international markets: Germany (559k CNC workers) and Asia (largest region) are underpenetrated

final_assessment.verdict: The claim of 20k-50k professional machinists paying for feeds/speeds calculators is PROBABLY ACCURATE for the high end, but likely represents 20k-35k reality for the lower-to-middle range. This represents ~6-12% of the US professional machinist base, which is reasonable for a specialized tool.
final_assessment.uncertainty_remaining: HIGH - No vendor publicly discloses user numbers, so all estimates are inferred from indirect metrics. Could be 10% off either direction.
final_assessment.investment_signal: Market exists and is real, but requires strong product differentiation to capture share. 'Me-too' calculator will struggle. Success requires solving current unmet needs: cloud sync, CAM integration, accuracy confidence, or mobile/offline capabilities.
